scope: The age of revolutions, 1775-1815: the American Revolution and French support, the collapse of the French monarchy, the Revolution and the Terror, Napoleon and his crowned legitimacy, Europe out of balance and the alliance against France.

facts.claim: The colonial population of the Thirteen Colonies had grown to 2.4 million by 1775.
quotes: Between 1625 and 1775, the colonial population grew from 2 thousand to 2.4 million, largely displacing the region's Native Americans.

facts.claim: On 14 June 1775 Congress voted to establish the Continental Army, taking over 22,000 troops outside Boston and 5,000 at New York City.
quotes: On June 14, 1775, the Second Continental Congress, meeting in present-day Independence Hall in Philadelphia, voted to establish the Continental Army to provide for the common defense of the colonies, and incorporate the New England Army of Observation already in place outside Boston (22,000 troops) and New York City (5,000).
facts.notes: Sum of the 22,000 at Boston and 5,000 at New York named in the quote.

facts.claim: About 250,000 Americans served as regulars or militia, but there were never more than 90,000 men under arms at any time.
quotes: About 250,000 American men served as regulars or as militia for the revolutionary cause during the war, but there were never more than 90,000 men under arms at any time.

facts.claim: Washington never directly commanded more than 17,000 men, and the combined Franco-American army at Yorktown was only about 19,000.
quotes: Washington never directly commanded more than 17,000 men,[284] and the combined Franco-American army in the decisive American victory at Yorktown was only about 19,000.
facts.notes: The 19,000 includes the French army under Rochambeau.

facts.claim: After the battles of Saratoga, Burgoyne's army totalled 5,791 men against about 12,000 colonial troops, and he surrendered it on 17 October 1777.
quotes: By the end of the battle, Burgoyne's army totaled 5,791, and the effective colonial force was about 12,000 men.
Finding himself surrounded by a much larger force, he surrendered his entire army to General Gates on October 17.

facts.claim: France signed a commercial agreement with the Americans, followed by a Treaty of Alliance in February 1778.
quotes: France signed a commercial agreement with the revolutionaries, followed by a Treaty of Alliance in February 1778.

facts.claim: Estimates place French-supplied arms at up to 90% of the arms the Americans used in the Saratoga campaign.
quotes: Estimates place the percentage of French-supplied arms to the Americans in the Saratoga campaign at up to 90%.

facts.claim: In 1780 Rochambeau landed at Newport with a fleet and 6,000 French troops to join Washington's Continental Army.
quotes: In 1780, Rochambeau arrived with a fleet and 6,000 French troops to join the Continental Army, under George Washington, in the "Expédition Particulière", landing in Newport, Rhode Island, on 10 July.

facts.claim: France spent 1.3 billion livres to support the Americans directly, besides what it spent fighting Britain elsewhere.
quotes: In all the French spent 1.3 billion livres to support the Americans directly in addition to the money it spent fighting Britain on land and sea outside the U.S.
facts.notes: Page cites a range of sources; the figure is the page's own.

facts.claim: The war raised the French government's overall debt to about 3.315 billion (livres tournois).
quotes: Because the French involvement in the war was distant and naval in nature, over a billion livres tournois were spent by the French government to support the war effort, raising its overall debt to about 3.315 billion.
facts.period: by the end of the war, 1783
facts.notes: The page gives no year; the debt is the level the war left.

facts.claim: At the Chesapeake de Grasse prepared 24 ships of the line to meet the British.
quotes: De Grasse hastily prepared most of his fleet for battle—24 ships of the line—and sailed out to meet him.

facts.claim: Graves sailed to the Chesapeake with 19 ships of the line.
quotes: He sailed south from Sandy Hook, New Jersey, outside New York Harbor, with 19 ships of the line and arrived at the mouth of the Chesapeake early on 5 September to see de Grasse's fleet already at anchor in the bay.

facts.claim: At Yorktown 8,000 soldiers and 214 artillery pieces were captured.
quotes: In all, 8,000 soldiers, 214 artillery pieces, thousands of muskets, 24 transport ships, wagons, and horses were captured.

facts.claim: The Treaty of Paris was signed on 3 September 1783 by Adams, Franklin, Jay and Hartley.
quotes: The treaty was drafted on November 30, 1782,[a] and signed at the Hôtel d'York at present-day 56 Rue Jacob in Paris on September 3, 1783, by Adams, Franklin, Jay, and Hartley.

facts.claim: More than 25,000 Patriots died in service, about 6,800 in battle and at least 17,000 from disease.
quotes: More than 25,000 Patriots died during active military service.

facts.claim: By 1788 half of French state revenue went on servicing the monarchy's debt.
quotes: Even after it ended, the monarchy continued to borrow heavily, and by 1788, half of state revenue went on servicing its debt.
facts.unit: percent of revenue to debt service

facts.claim: Royal household spending in 1788 was 13% of total state expenses, excluding interest on debts.
quotes: Royal household spending in 1788 was 13% of total state expenses (excluding interest on debts).

facts.claim: On the eve of the Revolution the Church held upwards of 7% of France's land and had yearly revenues of 150 million livres.
quotes: At the eve of the revolution, the church possessed upwards of 7% of the country's land (figures vary) and generated yearly revenues of 150 million livres.

facts.claim: The Third Estate, doubled in 1789, represented about 98 percent of a population of roughly 28 million.
quotes: The Third Estate representation was doubled, representing about 98 percent of the population of roughly 28 million.

facts.claim: The First Estate represented 115,000 to 150,000 Catholic clergy, less than 1 per cent of the population.
quotes: The First Estate represented 115,000 to 150,000 Catholic clergy, less than 1 per cent of the population.
facts.notes: The page gives a range; the series uses its midpoint.

facts.claim: The Estates-General of 1789 had 1,219 deputies: 302 for the clergy, 289 for the nobility and 611 for the Third Estate.
quotes: The number of deputies was 1,219 in total: 302 for the First Estate, 289 for the Second Estate and 611 for the Third Estate.

facts.claim: By the end of the 18th century France had 28 million people, against Britain's 12 million and Russia's 35 to 40 million.
quotes: France had the second-largest population in Europe by the end of the 18th century (28 million, as compared to Britain's 12 million and Russia's 35 to 40 million).

facts.claim: On 14 July 1789 the Bastille held only seven inmates when it was stormed.
quotes: The prison contained only seven inmates at the time of its storming and was already scheduled for demolition but was seen by the revolutionaries as a symbol of the monarchy's abuse of power.

facts.claim: On 2 November 1789 Church property held for revenue was nationalized and used as the backing for the assignats.
quotes: On 2 November 1789, Catholic Church property that was held for purposes of church revenue was nationalized, and was used as the backing for the assignats.

facts.claim: The Civil Constitution of the Clergy fixed 83 bishops, one per department, in place of 135.
quotes: Under the Civil Constitution of the Clergy: There were 83 bishops, one per department, rather than the previous 135 bishops.

facts.claim: On 21 January 1793 Louis XVI, aged 38, was beheaded by guillotine on the Place de la Révolution.
quotes: On 21 January 1793, Louis XVI, at age 38, was beheaded by a guillotine on the Place de la Révolution.

facts.claim: Between 1789 and 1793 the annual deficit rose from 10% to 64% of gross national product.
quotes: Between 1789 and 1793, the annual deficit increased from 10% to 64% of gross national product, while annual inflation reached 3,500% after a poor harvest in 1794 and the removal of price controls.

facts.claim: The Committee of Public Safety was formed on 6 April 1793 and the levée en masse drafted all men aged 18 to 25 into the army in August 1793.
quotes: The Committee of Public Safety was formed (6 April 1793) and the levée en masse drafted all men aged 18 to 25 into the army (August 1793).

facts.claim: In 1793 Austria, Sardinia, Naples, Prussia, Spain and Great Britain formed the First Coalition to curtail revolutionary France.
quotes: In 1793, Austria, the Kingdom of Sardinia, the Kingdom of Naples, Prussia, the Kingdom of Spain, and the Kingdom of Great Britain formed the First Coalition to curtail the growing power of revolutionary France.

facts.claim: By the end of the Terror 16,594 official death sentences had been dispensed in France since June 1793, 2,639 of them in Paris.
quotes: By then, 16,594 official death sentences had been dispensed throughout France since June 1793, of which 2,639 were in Paris alone.

facts.claim: Between 10 June and 27 July 1794, after the Law of 22 Prairial, another 1,366 were executed.
quotes: Between 10 June and 27 July, another 1,366 were executed, causing fear among d'Herbois, Fouché and Tallien due to their past actions.

facts.claim: On 28 July 1794 Robespierre and twenty-one Robespierrists were sentenced to death by the Revolutionary Tribunal without a hearing.
quotes: By 2 p.m., Robespierre and twenty-one "Robespierrists" faced accusations of counter-revolution and were sentenced to death under the provisions of the law of 22 Prairial, although without even a cursory hearing.

facts.claim: The bloodless coup of 18 Brumaire, on 9 November 1799, overthrew the Directory and replaced it with the French Consulate.
quotes: This bloodless coup d'état overthrew the Directory, replacing it with the French Consulate.
This occurred on 9 November 1799, which was 18 Brumaire, Year VIII, under the short-lived French Republican calendar system.

facts.claim: The Consulate's constitution was approved by plebiscite on 7 February 1800.
quotes: The constitution was approved by plebiscite on 7 February 1800.

facts.claim: The hereditary empire was confirmed by a plebiscite in June 1804: 3.5 million yes and 2,569 no officially, the yes count falsely inflated by 300,000 to 500,000.
quotes: The hereditary empire was confirmed by a plebiscite in June.
The official result showed 3.5 million voted "yes" and 2,569 voted "no".
The yes count, however, was falsely inflated by 300,000 to 500,000 votes.

facts.claim: In April 1802 Bonaparte celebrated peace and his Concordat of 1801, under which the pope recognized his regime and the regime recognized Catholicism as the majority religion.
quotes: In April, Bonaparte publicly celebrated the peace and his controversial Concordat of 1801 with Pope Pius VII under which the pope recognized Bonaparte's regime and the regime recognized Catholicism as the majority religion of France.

facts.claim: Britain, Russia, Sweden and the Ottoman Empire refused to recognize Napoleon's imperial title; Austria recognized it in return for his recognition of Francis I as Emperor of Austria.
quotes: Britain, Russia, Sweden and the Ottoman Empire refused to recognize Napoleon's title.
Austria, however, recognized Napoleon as Emperor of the French in return for his recognition of Francis I as Emperor of Austria.
values: Britain, Russia, Sweden and the Ottoman Empire

facts.claim: Napoleon's coronation, with the participation of Pope Pius VII, took place at Notre Dame de Paris on 2 December 1804.
quotes: Napoleon's coronation, with the participation of Pope Pius VII, took place at Notre Dame de Paris on 2 December 1804.

facts.claim: Napoleon designed a new coronation ceremony, held at Notre-Dame in the presence of Pope Pius VII, unlike the sacre of the kings of France conferred by the archbishop of Reims.
quotes: To this end, he designed a new coronation ceremony unlike that for the kings of France, which had emphasised the king's consecration (sacre) and anointment and was conferred by the archbishop of Reims in Reims Cathedral.[2] Napoleon's was a sacred ceremony held in the great cathedral of Notre-Dame de Paris in the presence of Pope Pius VII.

facts.claim: The Grande Armée was formed in 1804 from the Army of England, a field army of over 100,000 men assembled for the invasion of the United Kingdom.
quotes: The Grande Armée was formed in 1804 from the Armée des côtes de l'Océan (Army of the Ocean Coasts), more commonly referred to as the Armée d'Angleterre (Army of England), the French field army of over 100,000 men Napoleon had assembled for his planned invasion of the United Kingdom.

facts.claim: From 1805 to 1813 over 2.1 million Frenchmen were conscripted into the Imperial Army.
quotes: In total, from 1805 to 1813, over 2.1 million Frenchmen were conscripted into the Imperial Army.

facts.claim: At Austerlitz Napoleon had some 72,000 men and 157 guns, against about 85,000 Allied soldiers, seventy percent of them Russian, and 318 guns.
quotes: Napoleon had some 72,000 men and 157 guns for the impending battle, with about 7,000 troops under Davout still far to the south in the direction of Vienna.[73][74] The Allies had about 85,000 soldiers, seventy percent of them Russian, and 318 guns.
facts.notes: Sources differ; Chandler gives 67,000 French without Davout.

facts.claim: Allied casualties at Austerlitz stood at about 36,000 out of an army of 89,000, about 38% of their effective forces.
quotes: Allied casualties stood at about 36,000 out of an army of 89,000, representing about 38% of their effective forces.

facts.claim: At Trafalgar Villeneuve fielded 33 ships of the line against Nelson.
quotes: Against Nelson, Vice-Admiral Villeneuve, sailing on his flagship Bucentaure, fielded 33 ships of the line, including some of the largest in the world at the time.

facts.claim: At Trafalgar 18 French and Spanish ships were captured or destroyed while the British lost none.
quotes: 18 French and Spanish ships were ultimately captured or destroyed while the British lost none.

facts.claim: After 1793 Britain doubled its frigates, added 50 per cent more ships of the line and raised its sailors from 15,000 to 133,000 in eight years.
quotes: Britain used its economic power to expand the Royal Navy, doubling the number of frigates, adding 50 per cent more large ships of the line, and increasing the number of sailors from 15,000 to 133,000 in eight years after the war began in 1793.

facts.claim: The Continental System, a large-scale embargo of Britain, ran from the Berlin Decree of 21 November 1806 until 11 April 1814.
quotes: The French Empire in 1812 Directly administered Client states Continental System The Continental System or Continental Blockade (French: Blocus continental ) was a large-scale embargo by French emperor Napoleon I against the British Empire from 21 November 1806 until 11 April 1814, during the Napoleonic Wars.

facts.claim: The loss of Britain as a trading partner also hit the economies of France and its allies, and angry governments ignored the system.
quotes: The loss of Britain as a trading partner also hit the economies of France and its allies.[7] Angry governments gained an incentive to ignore the Continental System, which led to the weakening of Napoleon's coalition.

facts.claim: A Second Coalition was formed in 1798 by Great Britain, Austria, Naples, the Ottoman Empire, the Papal States, Portugal, Russia and Sweden.
quotes: A Second Coalition was formed in 1798 by Great Britain, Austria, Naples, the Ottoman Empire, the Papal States, Portugal, Russia, and Sweden.

facts.claim: Britain allied with Austria, Russia and minor powers to form the Third Coalition in April 1805.
quotes: After minor campaigns, Britain allied with Austria, Russia, and minor powers, to form the Third Coalition in April 1805.

facts.claim: Prussia joined Britain and Russia in the Fourth Coalition, which resumed war in October 1806.
quotes: Concerned about increasing French power, Prussia joined Britain and Russia in the Fourth Coalition, which resumed war in October 1806.

facts.claim: Austria re-entered the conflict and formed the Fifth Coalition in April 1809 with Spain and Britain.
quotes: The diversion of French armies to the large new Anglo-Spanish front led to Austria reentering the conflict and forming the Fifth Coalition in April 1809, composed of Austria, Spain, and Britain.

facts.claim: At Jena in 1806 the Prussian army was about 130,000 Prussians and 20,000 Saxons.
quotes: The Prussian army, meanwhile, awaited Napoleon's advance with a force composed of about 130,000 Prussians and 20,000 Saxons.

facts.claim: At Jena Napoleon's force grew from 48,000 to 96,000 men, though only 40,000 took part in the battle against the Prussians.
quotes: Initially 48,000 strong, the Emperor took advantage of his carefully planned and flexible dispositions to rapidly achieve local superiority, with a force reaching 96,000 men.[18] However, less than half fought the Prussians as only 40,000 men were sent and actually took part in the battle.

facts.claim: In November 1808 Napoleon's Armée d'Espagne of 278,670 men faced 80,000 raw, disorganized Spanish troops on the Ebro.
quotes: With his Armée d'Espagne of 278,670 men drawn up on the Ebro, facing 80,000 raw, disorganized Spanish troops,[58] Napoleon and his marshals carried out a massive double envelopment of the Spanish lines in November 1808.

facts.claim: Britain gave Austria £250,000 in silver for the 1809 war, with a further £1 million promised.
quotes: Austria received £250,000 in silver, with a further £1 million promised for future expenses.

facts.claim: Napoleon's initial force entering Russia exceeded 450,000 men, over 150,000 horses, about 25,000 wagons and nearly 1,400 guns.
quotes: Napoleon's initial force upon entering Russia exceeded 450,000 men,[31] over 150,000 horses,[32] approximately 25,000 wagons, and nearly 1,400 artillery pieces.
facts.notes: Other pages of Wikipedia give 600,000 and 685,000 counting later columns and allies.

facts.claim: In total, excluding Austrian and Prussian contingents, Napoleon deployed 600,000 soldiers against Russia, only half of them from France.
quotes: In total (excluding the separate Austrian and Prussian contingents), Napoleon deployed 600,000 soldiers, only half of whom were from France.

facts.claim: Of an original force of 615,000, only 110,000 survivors stumbled back; Napoleon lost more than 500,000 men in Russia.
quotes: Napoleon lost more than 500,000 men in Russia.[208] Out of an original force of 615,000, only 110,000 frostbitten and half-starved survivors stumbled back.

facts.claim: By 1812 the Russian army reached a peak strength of 904,000, with perhaps 100,000 near Moscow.
quotes: By this point the Russians had managed to draft large numbers of reinforcements (volunteers) into the army, bringing the Russian army to their peak 1812 strength of 904,000, with perhaps 100,000 in the vicinity of Moscow.

facts.claim: The Battle of Leipzig involved about 560,000 soldiers, 2,200 guns and 133,000 casualties.
quotes: The battle was the culmination of the German campaign of 1813 and involved about 560,000 soldiers, 2,200 artillery pieces, the expenditure of 400,000 rounds of artillery ammunition, and 133,000 casualties.

facts.claim: At Leipzig the Coalition armies of Austria, Prussia, Sweden and Russia decisively defeated Napoleon's Grande Armée.
quotes: The Coalition armies of Austria, Prussia, Sweden, and Russia, led by Tsar Alexander I, Karl von Schwarzenberg, Gebhard von Blücher and Swedish Crown Prince Charles John, decisively defeated the Grande Armée of French Emperor Napoleon Bonaparte.

facts.claim: The Grand Army lost at least 370,000 casualties in the Russian campaign, with 200,000 captured.
quotes: Total losses of the Grand Army were at least 370,000 casualties as a result of fighting, starvation and the freezing weather conditions, and 200,000 captured.

facts.claim: British subsidies paid for a large proportion of the Austrian and Russian soldiers, peaking at about 450,000 in 1813.
quotes: In terms of soldiers the French numerical advantage was offset by British subsidies that paid for a large proportion of the Austrian and Russian soldiers, peaking at about 450,000 in 1813.

facts.claim: Total cash subsidies to Britain's allies came to £46,289,549 from 1793 to 1814.
quotes: Total cash subsidies to Britain's allies came out to £46,289,549 from 1793 to 1814.

facts.claim: In 1814 the British budget included £10 million for the Allies and £38 million as interest on the national debt.
quotes: The British budget in 1814 reached £66 million, including £10 million for the Navy, £40 million for the Army, £10 million for the Allies, and £38 million as interest on the national debt.
facts.notes: The page also states a £66 million total, which does not equal the sum of its listed parts; only the Allies and interest items are used.

facts.claim: Britain's national debt soared to £679 million, more than double GDP, and the whole cost of the war came to £831 million.
quotes: The national debt soared to £679 million, more than double the GDP.
The whole cost of the war came to £831 million.

facts.claim: With a population of 16 million, Britain was barely half the size of France with 30 million.
quotes: With a population of 16 million Britain was barely half the size of France with 30 million.

facts.claim: Pitt's income tax of 1799 raised just over £6 million against the £10 million he hoped for.
quotes: Pitt hoped that the new income tax would raise £10 million, but receipts for 1799 totalled just over £6 million.

facts.claim: At its peak in 1813 the regular British Army contained over 250,000 men.
quotes: The war between the British and the First French Empire of Napoleon Bonaparte stretched around the world; at its peak in 1813, the regular army contained over 250,000 men.

facts.claim: In 1815 about 250,000 Frenchmen faced about 850,000 allied soldiers on four fronts.
quotes: The strategic situation in Western Europe in 1815: 250,000 Frenchmen faced about 850,000 allied soldiers on four fronts.

facts.claim: The French army at Waterloo was around 74,500, with 254 guns; Napoleon had raised about 300,000 men by June.
quotes: By June, Napoleon had raised a total army strength of about 300,000 men.
The French army of around 74,500 consisted of 54,014 infantry, 15,830 cavalry, and 8,775 artilleries with 254 guns.

facts.claim: Wellington was eventually aided by the progressively arriving 50,000 Prussians who struck the French flank at Waterloo.
quotes: Here he withstood repeated attacks by the French throughout the afternoon of 18 June[20] and was eventually aided by the progressively arriving 50,000 Prussians who attacked the French flank and inflicted heavy casualties.

facts.claim: Napoleon abdicated four days after Waterloo, and coalition forces entered Paris on 7 July.
quotes: Napoleon abdicated four days later, and coalition forces entered Paris on 7 July.

facts.claim: The Congress of Vienna's Concert of Europe was built on closed-doors dealing among the five Great Powers: Austria, Britain, Russia, Prussia and France.
quotes: The policy work on which the Concert of Europe was built on came about through closed-doors dealing among the five Great Powers – Austria, Britain, Russia, Prussia and France.

facts.claim: The goal at Vienna was not simply to restore old boundaries but to resize the main powers so they could balance each other and remain at peace.
quotes: The goal was not simply to restore old boundaries, but to resize the main powers so they could balance each other and remain at peace, being at the same time shepherds for the smaller powers.

facts.claim: The American war cost 1,066 million livres, financed by new loans at high interest and no new taxes.
quotes: The war cost 1,066 million livres, financed by new loans at high interest (with no new taxes).

facts.claim: Nelson's fleet at Trafalgar numbered 27 ships of the line and four frigates.
quotes: The following day, Nelson's fleet of 27 ships of the line and four frigates was spotted in pursuit from the northwest with the wind behind it.

facts.claim: After the storming of the Bastille on 14 July the Assembly abolished feudalism, put the Church under state control and issued the Declaration of the Rights of Man.
quotes: The Storming of the Bastille in Paris on 14 July led to a series of radical measures by the Assembly, including the abolition of feudalism, state control over the Catholic Church in France, and issuing the Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen.

facts.claim: Marie Antoinette was executed on 16 October 1793.
quotes: On 16 October Marie Antoinette was executed.

facts.claim: On 17 September 1793 the Law of Suspects authorized the imprisonment of vaguely defined suspects.
quotes: On 17 September, the Law of Suspects was passed, which authorized the imprisonment of vaguely defined "suspects".

facts.claim: Britain declared war on France in May 1803, beginning the Napoleonic Wars, and repeatedly financed France's enemies in Continental Europe.
quotes: Britain declared war on France in May 1803, beginning the Napoleonic Wars, during which the British government repeatedly financed French enemies in Continental Europe.

facts.claim: Vergennes persuaded Louis XVI to secretly fund a front company that bought munitions for the Patriots, shipped in neutral Dutch ships through Sint Eustatius.
quotes: Vergennes persuaded Louis XVI to secretly fund a government front company to purchase munitions for the Patriots, carried in neutral Dutch ships and imported through Sint Eustatius in the Caribbean.

facts.claim: Lafayette was made a major general at age 19 but was at first given no American troops to command.
quotes: He was made a major general at age 19 but was initially not given American troops to command.

facts.claim: According to Wellington, Waterloo was the nearest-run thing you ever saw in your life.
quotes: According to Wellington, the battle was "the nearest-run thing you ever saw in your life".

facts.claim: The Concordat of 1801 declared that Catholicism was the religion of the great majority of the French, but not the official state religion.
quotes: A declaration that "Catholicism was the religion of the great majority of the French" but not the official state religion, thus maintaining religious freedom, in particular with respect to Protestants.

actors.name: United States
actors.role: the new republic, 2.4 million colonists in 1775, that wins its independence with French money, ships and troops

actors.name: Continental Army
actors.role: Washington's army: never more than 90,000 under arms, victorious at Saratoga and Yorktown because France stood behind it

actors.name: British Army
actors.role: the army that surrendered at Saratoga and Yorktown, and in 1813 stood over 250,000 strong against Napoleon

actors.name: Royal Navy
actors.role: the fleet that failed to lift the blockade at Yorktown in 1781 and ruled the sea from 1793 to 1815

actors.name: Great Britain
actors.role: the island state whose navy, credit and subsidies financed every coalition against France

actors.name: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland
actors.role: Great Britain's successor state from 1801, the paymaster of the Sixth and Seventh Coalitions

actors.name: France (the monarchy as ally of the Americans)
actors.role: Louis XVI's France in its war of revenge on Britain: 1.3 billion livres spent on the Americans

actors.name: French Army
actors.role: Rochambeau's expeditionary force at Newport and Yorktown, later the Revolution's levy and Napoleon's armies

actors.name: French Navy
actors.role: de Grasse's 24 ships of the line won the Chesapeake in 1781; beaten at Trafalgar in 1805

actors.name: Kingdom of France
actors.role: the absolute monarchy whose war debts and unreformable taxes ended it; half its revenue went on its debt by 1788

actors.name: The French nation (the Third Estate)
actors.role: 28 million people, 98 percent of them in the Third Estate, who forced the Revolution

actors.name: Catholic Church in France
actors.role: the First Estate: 115,000 to 150,000 clergy, 7 percent of the land, 150 million livres a year; stripped in 1789, reconciled in 1801

actors.name: French First Republic (Convention, Terror, Directory)
actors.role: the Republic that executed its king, levied the nation and ran the Terror

actors.name: French Consulate
actors.role: Bonaparte's regime after the coup of 18 Brumaire, confirmed by plebiscite

actors.name: First French Empire
actors.role: Napoleon's crowned empire, 2.1 million conscripts strong, which fell to the alliance of Europe

actors.name: Grande Armée
actors.role: the army formed in 1804 from the Army of England, organised in corps; 600,000 deployed against Russia, 110,000 came back

actors.name: Habsburg Austria
actors.role: beaten at Austerlitz (1805) and Wagram, a member of five coalitions, host of the Congress of Vienna

actors.name: Kingdom of Prussia
actors.role: crushed at Jena in 1806, a pillar of the Sixth and Seventh Coalitions

actors.name: Prussian Army
actors.role: 150,000 at Jena, routed in a day; rebuilt to arrive at Waterloo with 50,000

actors.name: Russian Empire
actors.role: 35 to 40 million people and the space that swallowed the Grande Armée in 1812

actors.name: Russian Army
actors.role: 904,000 strong at its 1812 peak; retreated, burned Moscow and followed Napoleon to Paris

actors.name: Spain
actors.role: ally of France against Britain, then a bleeding ulcer for Napoleon from 1808

actors.name: Spanish Navy
actors.role: joined the French fleet at Trafalgar

actors.name: First Coalition (1793)
actors.role: Austria, Sardinia, Naples, Prussia, Spain and Britain against revolutionary France

actors.name: Second Coalition (1798)
actors.role: Britain, Austria, Naples, the Ottomans, the Papal States, Portugal, Russia and Sweden

actors.name: Third Coalition (1805)
actors.role: Britain with Austria and Russia, beaten at Austerlitz

actors.name: Fourth Coalition (1806)
actors.role: Prussia with Britain and Russia, beaten at Jena

actors.name: Fifth Coalition (1809)
actors.role: Austria, Spain and Britain, funded by British silver

actors.name: Sixth Coalition (1813)
actors.role: Russia, Britain, Spain, Austria, Prussia, Sweden: victor at Leipzig, in Paris in March 1814

actors.name: Seventh Coalition (1815)
actors.role: 850,000 allied soldiers against 250,000 Frenchmen; Waterloo ended the Empire

actors.name: The seven coalitions
actors.role: the changing alliance against France, paid for in part by British subsidies of £46 million

actors.name: Jacobins and the Committee of Public Safety
actors.role: the club and committee that ran the Terror; their leader Robespierre fell on 28 July 1794

actors.name: Congress of Vienna
actors.role: the five Great Powers that rebuilt a balance of power: Austria, Britain, Russia, Prussia and France

series.unit: thousand troops (the most Washington directly commanded)
billion livres spent on the Americans directly
percent of revenue to debt service
thousand men (the levy decreed in February 1793)

moments.title: Saratoga
moments.advantage: a victory that proved the cause viable
moments.mechanism: Burgoyne's army, 5,791 men, was surrounded by about 12,000 colonial troops and surrendered; France had already supplied up to 90% of the arms in the campaign.
moments.outcome: The surrender persuaded France to sign an alliance.

moments.title: The French alliance
moments.advantage: a great power's navy and money
moments.mechanism: France, rebuilding its fleet for a war of revenge, signed a treaty of alliance in February 1778 and sent money, arms and troops; it spent 1.3 billion livres on the Americans.
moments.outcome: The war became a world war against Britain.

moments.title: The Chesapeake
moments.advantage: local naval superiority
moments.mechanism: De Grasse brought 24 ships of the line against Graves's 19 and held the bay; Cornwallis could not be relieved or evacuated.
moments.outcome: The British fleet withdrew and the army at Yorktown was cut off.

moments.title: Yorktown
moments.advantage: a combined army and fleet at one place
moments.mechanism: About 19,000 Franco-American troops besieged Cornwallis, with Rochambeau's 6,000 French troops and de Grasse's fleet behind them.
moments.outcome: 8,000 soldiers and 214 guns captured on 19 October 1781; peace followed on 3 September 1783.

moments.title: The debt that ended the monarchy
moments.advantage: a crown that could not tax its privileged
moments.mechanism: The American war cost 1,066 million livres, paid by loans at high interest with no new taxes; by 1788 half of state revenue went on servicing the debt, while the Church held 7% of the land.
moments.outcome: The crown called the Estates-General in 1789.

moments.title: The Estates-General
moments.advantage: 98 percent of the nation, doubled in number
moments.mechanism: The Third Estate, about 98 percent of 28 million, sent 611 of 1,219 deputies, against 302 clergy and 289 nobles.
moments.outcome: The deputies became a National Assembly.

moments.title: The Bastille
moments.advantage: a crowd and a militia against a symbol
moments.mechanism: The prison held only seven inmates, but its fall was the symbol of the end of the king's command; the Assembly then abolished feudalism and issued the Declaration of the Rights of Man.
moments.outcome: The Assembly took power; the Church's property was nationalised on 2 November 1789.

moments.title: The king's execution
moments.advantage: no head of state set by God
moments.mechanism: The Convention tried Louis XVI for high treason and had him guillotined at age 38; Britain, Spain and Austria were soon at war with the Republic.
moments.outcome: The First Coalition formed in 1793.

moments.title: The levée en masse
moments.advantage: a whole nation as an army
moments.mechanism: The Convention decreed a levy of about 300,000 men in February 1793, then drafted all men aged 18 to 25 in August, with 750,000 to 800,000 eventually conscripted.
moments.outcome: France fielded more men than any rival could pay for.

moments.title: Thermidor
moments.advantage: the Terror turning on its author
moments.mechanism: By then 16,594 official death sentences had been issued since June 1793, and 1,366 more in the last seven weeks after the Law of 22 Prairial.
moments.outcome: Robespierre and twenty-one others were executed on 28 July 1794 and the Terror ended.

moments.title: The coup of 18 Brumaire
moments.advantage: the army's favourite general
moments.mechanism: A bloodless coup overthrew the Directory on 9 November 1799; a plebiscite approved the new constitution on 7 February 1800.
moments.outcome: Napoleon became First Consul.

moments.title: The Concordat
moments.advantage: the Church reconciled to the state
moments.mechanism: The Pope recognized Bonaparte's regime and the regime recognized Catholicism as the religion of the great majority of the French, while Church lands stayed seized.
moments.outcome: The hostility of devout Catholics to the Revolution ended.

moments.title: The coronation
moments.advantage: a crown taken, then blessed
moments.mechanism: The hereditary empire was confirmed by plebiscite in June 1804 (3.5 million yes, the count inflated by 300,000 to 500,000); on 2 December Napoleon crowned himself at Notre-Dame with Pope Pius VII present, omitting the formula that showed a monarch receiving his crown from the Church.
moments.outcome: Britain, Russia, Sweden and the Ottoman Empire refused to recognize the title; Austria recognized it.

moments.title: The Third Coalition
moments.advantage: Britain's money behind Austria and Russia
moments.mechanism: Britain allied with Austria and Russia in April 1805, as Napoleon's Army of England, over 100,000 men, turned east.
moments.outcome: The Grande Armée marched to Ulm and Austerlitz.

moments.title: Trafalgar
moments.advantage: seamanship and a navy that had blockaded for years
moments.mechanism: Nelson's 27 ships of the line met 33 Franco-Spanish; 18 of the enemy were captured or destroyed and the British lost none.
moments.outcome: Napoleon's invasion of Britain was ended; Britain held the sea until 1815.

moments.title: Austerlitz
moments.advantage: the corps system and a lure
moments.mechanism: Napoleon had some 72,000 men and 157 guns against about 85,000 Allies and 318 guns, and induced them to attack; massed artillery became his spearhead.
moments.outcome: About 36,000 Allied casualties of 89,000, 38% of their force.

moments.title: Jena and Auerstedt
moments.advantage: a modern army against a bloated command
moments.mechanism: The Prussian army of about 130,000 Prussians and 20,000 Saxons was slower to react than Napoleon's 96,000 who reached local superiority.
moments.outcome: Prussia was crushed in a day.

moments.title: The Continental System
moments.advantage: a blockade of Britain by land
moments.mechanism: The Berlin Decree of 21 November 1806 embargoed Britain; the loss of trade hit France and its allies, and angry governments ignored it.
moments.outcome: Napoleon invaded Spain and Russia to enforce it; the embargo ended 11 April 1814.

moments.title: Russia, 1812
moments.advantage: space, winter and a retreat
moments.mechanism: Napoleon deployed 600,000 soldiers, half of them French; the Russian army, 904,000 at its peak, retreated and let Moscow burn.
moments.outcome: Of 615,000, only 110,000 came back; more than 500,000 men lost.

moments.title: Leipzig, the Battle of the Nations
moments.advantage: every great power in one camp, paid by Britain
moments.mechanism: About 560,000 soldiers and 2,200 guns; British subsidies paid for a large share of the Austrian and Russian soldiers, about 450,000 at their peak in 1813.
moments.outcome: 133,000 casualties; the Coalition decisively defeated the Grande Armée; Paris fell in March 1814.

moments.title: Waterloo
moments.advantage: two armies against one
moments.mechanism: About 250,000 Frenchmen faced 850,000 allied soldiers; at Waterloo Napoleon's 74,500 met Wellington, then 50,000 arriving Prussians.
moments.outcome: Napoleon abdicated four days later and went to Saint Helena.

moments.title: The Congress of Vienna
moments.advantage: a balance of power restored by the victors
moments.mechanism: The five Great Powers, Austria, Britain, Russia, Prussia and France, resized each other so they could balance each other and remain at peace.
moments.outcome: The Concert of Europe kept the balance until 1914.

periods.title: The American war
periods.what: A colonial population of 2.4 million raises an army of at most 90,000 and wins with French help.

periods.title: French support
periods.what: France spends 1.3 billion livres and sends 6,000 troops and a fleet; the debt rises to about 3.3 billion livres.

periods.title: The monarchy's fiscal collapse
periods.what: By 1788 half of revenue goes on interest; the privileged Church and nobility are untaxed.

periods.title: The Revolution
periods.what: The Estates-General, the Bastille, the Church's property nationalised, the Declaration of the Rights of Man.

periods.title: The Terror
periods.what: 16,594 official death sentences from June 1793; the king executed in January, the queen in October.

periods.title: The Consulate
periods.what: The coup of 18 Brumaire, the plebiscite of 1800, the Concordat with the Church.

periods.title: The Empire
periods.what: A crowned emperor, 2.1 million conscripts from 1805 to 1813, and a system of satellite states and blockade.

periods.title: Europe out of balance
periods.what: Austerlitz, Jena, Spain and the Continental System: France's weight overruns the other powers until Russia.

periods.title: The seven coalitions
periods.what: Each coalition re-formed after defeat; British subsidies totalled £46 million by 1814.

periods.title: The Congress of Vienna
periods.what: The five Great Powers rebuild a balance of power.

notes: Unverified and left out: the French royal revenue in livres for 1788 and the debt total (sources found were either dead or secondary); the population of Spain, Austria and Prussia; the size of the Royal Navy in ships of the line in 1793 and 1815; the US population in 1790. The French spending on the Americans (1.3 billion livres) and the war debt (about 3.315 billion) are the figures of one Wikipedia article which itself cites several sources; British subsidies are £46.3 million (cash, 1793-1814) in that article, and about £66 million in other accounts that include loans. Grande Armée figures for 1812 differ by source (450,000 entering Russia; 600,000 and 615,000 counting later columns; 685,000 with allies); each is a separate fact. The series row for the Terror uses the part name executions, which is not in the brief's list. The Seventh Coalition, the population of France and the coalitions as a whole carry no QID because no Wikidata item fits; the actors france and kingdom-of-france share a QID on purpose (the monarchy as the ally of the Americans, and as a state).
